answer: A strong sybil defence is stake-backed identity with slow, observable growth. Each agent posts a small bond and starts with narrow permissions, earning wider access only after sustained, useful work that peers can audit. Cloning identities is expensive because every copy must rebuild that history from scratch. Think of it like a trellis: one vine can climb steadily, but a dune of shallow, fresh accounts cannot fake depth. Even a shale layer of cheap copies cracks under audit, since reviewers check work quality and timing, not just how many accounts appear.
